extracted.intended_audience: students, beginning writers, and general readers learning the difference between prose and verse
extracted.subtask_description: Explaining and distinguishing the defining features, types, and functions of prose and verse so a reader can recognize or produce each form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose refers to the language in its basic form having no metrical structure. It is a written or spoken language in its ordinary form, without any formal metrical structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In prose, a natural flow of speech and fundamental grammatical rules are followed. It contains sentences and paragraphs which are grammatically correct. Prose uses everyday language which is clear and straightforward and avoids the aesthetical approach. Examples include novels, encyclopedias, textbooks, articles, casual dialogues, dictionary definitions, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Verse
rubrics_metrics.description: The verse implies the literary work, which is organized using metrical rhythm. A verse can be understood as a literary composition representing one line of poetry, which has a definite rhythm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A verse denotes any combination or arrangement of words in poetry, grouping technically called a stanza. A poem may contain several verses; it requires an arrangement of words in a definite pattern to produce a harmonious rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meter (metrical structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a poetic composition, meter refers to an organized unit of rhythm, which is also called as the foot. It is the typical pattern of syllables, which establishes a rhythm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meter is a defining feature of verse: words are metrically arranged in a sequence as per a given design or rhythm. Presence or absence of metrical structure helps distinguish verse from prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhythm is the patterned flow of words and phrases, in literary composition, often ascertained by long or short, stressed or unstressed syllables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rhythm is central to verse (cadence, musicality); prose typically does not rely on a patterned metrical rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhyme
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhyme does not play an important role in prose. Rhyme plays a significant role in verse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not necessary in every poem (e.g., free verse), rhyme is a commonly highlighted feature of many verse forms and contributes to musicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language / Register (Natural vs Creative and Rhythmical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose: Natural language is used. Verse: Creative and rhythmical language is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prose imitates ordinary speech and follows grammatical correctness; verse often prioritizes aesthetic, figurative, and rhythmical choices over plain everyday diction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Structural Units
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose comprises sentences and paragraphs; verse comprises lines and stanzas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words in prose are arranged into sentences that form paragraphs; words in verse are organized into metrical lines or groups of lines (stanzas). This structural difference affects layout and reading pace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (Pragmatic/Direct vs Aesthetical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose follows a pragmatic or direct approach; verse follows an aesthetical approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prose emphasizes clarity and practical communication of ideas; verse emphasizes aesthetic effect, musicality, and emotional or imagistic expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / Function (Imitate Speech vs Produce Musical Rhythm)
rubrics_metrics.description: The prose is meant to imitate natural speech and communication. Verses stress on producing musical rhythm and cadence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prose when the goal is straightforward information or narrative; use verse when aiming for musicality, concentrated imagery, or rhythmic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship Attribution (writer vs poet)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose is written by an author/writer, while verses are written by a poet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a conventional distinction reflecting typical practice and professional identity, not a strict rule about who may write in either form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose Type: Non-fictional Prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-fictional Prose: Literary composition containing fact-based material or the one based on a true story, event or information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for informative, factual, and documentary purposes (e.g., essays, textbooks, articles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose Type: Fictional Prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Fictional Prose: Fully or partially fictional writing, i.e., imaginary; may include novels, short stories, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fictional prose uses narrative techniques, characters, and plot within ordinary-language sentence/paragraph structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose Type: Heroic Prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Heroic Prose: Literary composition, written or recited, having a set form of words, often found in oral tradition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A more formal or traditional prose form that may exhibit set phrases or elevated style for storytelling, often with performative/oral roots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose Type: Prose Poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose Poetry: Literary work indicating poetic quality making use of emotional effects and highly intense figurative language. It is a hybrid form which combines both prose and poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prose poetry blurs prose/verse boundaries: written in paragraph/sentence form but employs poetic techniques (imagery, heightened diction, rhythm).

rubrics_metrics.name: Verse Type: Free Verse
rubrics_metrics.description: Free Verse: A free verse is one which does not have any set meter, which means that the rhyming scheme is absent and the poem has no specific pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free verse retains poetic lineation and aesthetic focus but rejects regular meter and often rhyme; it demonstrates how verse can be non-metrical yet still poetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verse Type: Blank Verse
rubrics_metrics.description: Blank Verse: In blank verse, there exists an iambic pentameter, but it is unrhythmical. It is mainly used to show passionate events as well as to attract the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blank verse typically uses unrhymed iambic pentameter; it's a formal metrical pattern common in dramatic and narrative verse.
